proposals.evidence: DEDR1159(a) gives Kurukh xann and Malto qanu eye. Survey Kurukh kʰann retains its fricative/aspirate transcription. The Malto annotation explicitly notes that Andronov initial q corresponds to zero or a possible glottal stop in this list, supporting a comparative āndu proposal while retaining the unexplained-looking final material for review. No source spelling is repaired. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1630 directly gives Malto kuku ‘head’, alongside Kurukh kukk. Survey kukudu ‘head’ is a comparative form with the final -du retained; the proposed link concerns the kuku- stem rather than inventing a new parent. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
